rows.name: DEPLOY_REPO_URL
rows.values: Git URL of the repository. The script gives the text to `git clone` unchanged. The workflows write `https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/<repository>.git`.
rows.default: Unset: the script prints `DEPLOY_REPO_URL environment variable must be set` and exits with status 1. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: The script clones the `gh-pages` branch from this URL. It replaces one directory of the branch with the given report directory. It commits the result and pushes it to the same URL.
rows.notes: The script also writes a new `index.html` at the top of the branch. The workflows put the GitHub token of the workflow run into the URL.

evidence.quote: echo "DEPLOY_REPO_URL environment variable must be set" >&2

rows.name: DISPATCH_CHANNEL
rows.values: `unstable` or `testing`, the choices of the workflow input `channel`. Other text that is not empty stops a manual run with `Unknown apt channel`.
rows.default: Unset: no channel is requested. A tag ref selects `testing`. Every other ref selects `unstable`. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: The script uses the value only when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` is `workflow_dispatch` (a manual run). The value then selects the APT channel (a package set of the Positron APT server) for the `tron` package.
rows.notes: `testing` is refused when the ref is neither a tag nor a feature branch (a branch other than `main` and `release-*`). A feature branch also needs `FEATURE_TESTING_PUBLISH` set to `1`. The input default is `unstable`.

evidence.quote: printf 'Unknown apt channel %q: expected unstable or testing.\n' \

rows.name: DRY_RUN
rows.values: `true` or `false`, from the manual run input `dry_run`. The steps pass it to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument. Other text stops that script with `invalid dry-run state`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. Both jobs define it. A scheduled run gets `false`. The input default of a manual run is `true`.
rows.effect: `true` marks a dry run of the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again). The job `refresh` skips the default branch checkout. It uses `config/test-benchmarks.json` of the measured commit as base.
rows.notes: With `false`, a manual run stops unless the branch is the default branch and the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED` is `true`. The job `publish` opens the pull request. That job tests the input `dry_run` directly, not this variable.

rows.name: ENABLE_2X72
rows.values: Text of the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED`. Only the exact text `true` enables. All other text counts as not enabled.
rows.default: Unset: the job always defines it. An undefined repository variable gives an empty value. Empty counts as not enabled.
rows.effect: `true` adds the runner class `2x72core` (one kind of benchmark runner) to the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again). Without `true`, a request for `all` refreshes only `2x96core`.
rows.notes: The steps pass the value to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument. Without `true`, a request for `2x72core` stops the job `plan` with `2x72core refreshes are disabled`. The request is the manual run input `runner_class`. A scheduled run requests `all`.

rows.name: EXPECTED_BITFILE
rows.who_sets: `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`. A person who follows the manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` sets it by hand.
rows.read_by: The step `Quiesce and run full slice cost-data measurement` of the job `refresh` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). The shell commands of the manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` also read it.
rows.values: Bitfile identity `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>`. The release code is 4 hexadecimal pairs joined by dots. The text comes from the repository variable `SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X96CORE` or `SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE`. Letter case is ignored.
rows.default: Unset: the bitfile identity is not compared. An empty value does the same. An undefined repository variable gives an empty value.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` gets the value as an argument. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` reads the bitfile identity of every FPGA card of the runner before the measurement. It stops with `bitfile mismatch` when the identity differs from this value.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` also stops when the FPGA cards hold different bitfiles. That check does not need this value. The manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` reads the same name and stops when it is unset or empty.

rows.name: EXPECTED_RUNNER_CLASSES
rows.read_by: The step `Check latest scheduled refresh jobs` of the job `health` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`).
rows.values: Runner class names with spaces between them. The workflow writes `2x96core 2x72core` when the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED` is `true`. Otherwise it writes `2x96core`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The job always defines it.
rows.effect: The health check (`bin/ci/bench_refresh_health.py`) looks at the runs of `bench-refresh.yml` from the last 14 days. It fails unless each named runner class (one kind of benchmark runner) has a measured and published refresh.
rows.notes: The step passes the value without quotes to `bin/ci/bench_refresh_health.py`. Each word becomes one argument of `--expected-runner-classes`. A name that `bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py` does not list stops the health check with `unknown runner class`. Only runs on the default branch count.

rows.name: EXPECTED_SHA7
rows.read_by: The step `Verify build content hash` of the jobs `test-host` and `test-fpga` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`)
rows.values: 7 hexadecimal characters from the job `build`. They are the start of the SHA-256 hash of the `git ls-files -s` output, without the entry for the top-level `compile_commands.json`.
rows.default: Unset: the step always defines it. An empty value makes the comparison fail.
rows.effect: The step compares the value with the same hash of its own checkout. The step fails when the two differ.
rows.notes: The value is a hash of the tracked files. It is not a Git commit id.

rows.name: FEATURE_TESTING_PUBLISH
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` allows the publish. All other text refuses it. The workflow writes `0`.
rows.default: Unset: the same as `0`. The script refuses a feature-branch publish to `testing` and exits with status 1.
rows.effect: `1` lets a manual run publish a feature branch (a branch other than `main` and `release-*`) to the APT channel `testing` (a package set of the Positron APT server).
rows.notes: Tag pushes and the channel `unstable` do not need it. `main` and `release-*` branches are refused for `testing` with any value. A workflow comment says to write `1` only after the APT server keeps `~feature.` versions apart from the test candidates.

rows.name: GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME
rows.values: Directory name without a path. The workflow writes `gcp-nix-<run id>-<run attempt>-<job id>`.
rows.default: Unset: the workflow always defines it. The cleanup step uses `${GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME:?}`. An unset or empty value stops its `rm` command with an error.
rows.effect: It names the temporary directory of one job: `$RUNNER_TEMP/$GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME`. The job keeps its Nix result links and other temporary files there. The last step of the job removes the directory.
rows.notes: `JOB_TEMP` holds the full path of the same directory. `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` sets the name to `job` when it runs 3 steps of the job `tron-build`.

rows.name: GIT_SHA7
rows.read_by: The step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of the job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`).
rows.values: Short Git commit id of the checkout. The step `Identify checked-out commit` writes it with `git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD`. `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` keeps the first 7 characters.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The step always defines it.
rows.effect: The step passes the value to `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`. That script uses it in the name of the benchmark result file: `<results directory>/<value>.<host>.json`. The results directory is `/scratch/tron-benchmark` unless `TRON_BENCHMARK_RESULTS_ROOT` is set.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` has a script variable of the same name. That script takes the value from its second argument, not from the environment.

rows.name: HEALTH_REPORT
rows.read_by: The step `Reconcile slice refresh health issue` of the job `reconcile` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`).
rows.values: `healthy`, `stale:<platform names with commas>` or `probe-error:<error name>`. It is the output `report` of the job `health`. Other text counts as no valid report.
rows.default: Unset: the job always defines it. An empty value counts as no valid report.
rows.effect: `healthy` together with a successful job `health` closes the open GitHub issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy`. In every other case `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` opens that issue or adds a comment to it.
rows.notes: The step passes the report and the result of the job `health` to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`. A `stale:` or `probe-error:` report is valid only with the result `failure`. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_health.py` writes the report. The platform names are `genoa96` for the `2x96core` runners and `granite_rapids_6962p` for the `2x72core` runners.

evidence.quote: diagnosis="Probe error: health job returned no valid report."

rows.name: INGEST_STORE_PATH
rows.values: Nix store path of the ingest executable, of the form `/nix/store/<hash>-<name>`. It is the output `store_path` of the job `build-ingest`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. Both jobs define it.
rows.effect: The jobs fetch this store path from the Nix binary cache at `REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE` with `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py`. The ingest tests run `<value>/bin/ingest`. The plugin build gets the value as the Nix argument `ingest`.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py` rejects text that is not a Nix store path of the form `/nix/store/<hash>-<name>`.

rows.name: JOB_RESULTS
rows.values: JSON object, parsed with `json.loads`. Each key is a job name. Each value is an object with a `result` field. The workflow writes `toJSON(needs)`.
rows.default: Unset: the script prints `'JOB_RESULTS'` and exits with status 1.
rows.effect: The script exits with status 0 only when every job has the result `success`. Otherwise it prints the jobs that did not succeed and exits with status 1.
rows.notes: Text that is not JSON and an empty object also give exit status 1. In `gcp-nix.yml` the job `test` checks the jobs `tron-build`, `test-host` and `test-fpga` this way.

evidence.quote: raise ValueError("No job results were supplied")

rows.name: POSITRON_APT_LOGIN_TOKEN
rows.who_sets: GitHub repository secret settings. `.github/workflows/deb-smoke.yml` and `.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml` copy the secret into the environment of one step.
rows.values: Secret login token for the APT server `apt.positron.internal`. The script writes the text unchanged after the word `login`.
rows.default: Unset: the script prints `FAIL: POSITRON_APT_LOGIN_TOKEN must be set` and exits with status 1. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: The script writes the token to a temporary file. It mounts the file read-only into the Ubuntu 22.04 test container as the APT login file `/etc/apt/auth.conf.d/positron.conf`.
rows.notes: The script unsets the variable before it starts `docker`. The token is not passed as a container environment variable. A workflow that calls `deb-smoke.yml` or `publish-deb.yml` must pass the secret. A person who runs the script by hand sets the variable first.

new_terms.definition: The workflow `bench-refresh.yml`. It measures the test times and the peak memory of the Slice tests again on a benchmark runner. It then opens or updates a pull request that changes `config/test-benchmarks.json`.
The runner label that selects one kind of benchmark runner. The two classes are `2x96core` and `2x72core`.

The text `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>` that `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` builds from the release code and the release date of the bitfile in an FPGA card. The release code is 4 pairs of hexadecimal digits with dots between them.
A named package set of the Positron APT server. `publish-deb.yml` publishes the `tron` Debian package to the channel `unstable` or `testing`.
For `bin/ci/resolve-apt-channel.sh`, a branch other than `main` and the `release-*` branches.
The files that the CI job `build-model-traces` exports for the test models with `bin/ci/model-traces/export.py`. The plugin build reads them with the ingest executable.
The model code that ingest generates. In CI the job `generate-plugins` builds it from the model traces.

The Nix store path that the CI job `prepare-tron-build-inputs` builds from `nix/tron-build.nix`. It links the build recipe of TRON, the inputs of that build, and the Python, test and benchmark environments. The job `tron-build` builds TRON from it.

A SHA-256 hash that `bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py` computes from the benchmark payload identity, the source hash, the machine class and the host name. `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` names the cached benchmark result file with it.
A path of the form `/nix/store/<hash>-<name>`. The hash has 32 characters. The path holds one build result of Nix.
A server that holds finished Nix build results. A CI job copies a Nix store path from it and does not build that path again.

notes: Short version: all 21 variables of chunk ci-02 have one row and none is dropped. No cell held a wrong default or a wrong accepted value. 18 rows changed, 14 of them in meaning. One cell was too broad: EXPECTED_SHA7 said that the hash leaves out `the compile_commands.json entries`, and the code leaves out only the top-level file. Added facts: the second condition of a manual run with DRY_RUN `false`, the form of the release code in EXPECTED_BITFILE, the default-branch rule of the health check, the platform names in HEALTH_REPORT, the store path check of `acquire.py` for the 3 store path variables, the script that fills MODEL_WEIGHTS_ROOT, and the manual use of EXPECTED_BITFILE and POSITRON_APT_LOGIN_TOKEN. Structure change in 12 rows: `read_by` now names only the workflow steps, and so only files that contain the variable name. The writer had also named the script that receives the value as an argument. That script is now named in `values`, `effect` or `notes` of the same row. DEPLOY_REPO_URL `effect` had 4 sentences. It now has 3. GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME, JOB_TEMP and LAB_NIX_CACHE now list `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` in `who_sets`. The test sets all three names. DISPATCH_CHANNEL, JOB_RESULTS and MACHINERY_RESULT are unchanged. Source choices kept from the writer: an env entry at job level is `workflow env`. JOB_TEMP is `step env`: a step appends it to the `GITHUB_ENV` file, and the draft rows SOURCE_HASH and TRACE_INPUTS of the chunks ci-03 and ci-04 use the same value for that case. Evidence: all 81 quotes were compared with the cited line of the checkout at commit 7eddde7895. 76 equal the whole line without indentation. 5 are an exact part of the line: bench-refresh-health.yml:44 holds a pipe character, and gcp-nix.yml:390 (2 quotes), gcp-nix.yml:432 and gcp-nix.yml:493 are longer than 120 characters. Two statements rest on GitHub behaviour that the checkout does not show in code: an undefined repository variable gives an empty value (ENABLE_2X72, EXPECTED_BITFILE), and a job result is one of `success`, `failure`, `cancelled` or `skipped` (MACHINERY_RESULT). `doc/slice-benchmark-lifecycle.md` and `bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py` agree with both. New terms: `build plan`, `benchmark result identity`, `Nix store path` and `Nix binary cache`. The chunks ci-01, ci-03 and ci-04 define some of the same terms with other words, so the definitions need one merge.
